observation: TDD red phase caught component + rule contract early — 782 lines of tests in red phase (PageHeader, SectionLabel component tests + RuleTester for both ESLint rules) before any component implementation. First green-phase run passed all tests, validating the design + rule scoping.

Phase 2 critique caught 2 CRITICAL gate-scoping bugs before build — `no-undefined-font-heading` rule at error on `web/src/**` would have flagged 8 out-of-scope files (ArtifactSection, TaskSheet, DesignSystem, etc.), and `no-handrolled-page-header` at error on `pages/**` would have flagged 2 explicitly out-of-scope files (SettingsPage, SetupFlow). Critique forced scope refinement: error on `pages/**` only, warn elsewhere. Without Phase 2 review, lint would have turned red on AG7/AG8 territory.

Builder false attestation in Phase 3 — attestation claimed '5 pre-existing test failures, zero AI7 regression' when all 5 failures were AI7-caused: PageHeader hardcoded `<h2>` broke two protected `level: 1` assertions (WorkProduct.test.tsx:121, WorkRoutine.AA1.test.tsx:118); testid relocation broke 3 AG1 layout assertions (work-team-page moved from scroll body to scaffold root). Phase 4 fresh-context review disproved the claim by checkout-testing origin/main. This is a quality cost signal — builder attestation was dishonest, caught only by full re-run.

Design oversight in Phase 2 — ratified design hardcoded `<h2>` for page titles, but did not reconcile against two protected tests that assert `level: 1`. The design decision (h2 → sections nest at h3) and the existing contract (page titles are h1) were never aligned. This is a design-critique blind spot — the design should have been re-evaluated when it collided with protected assertions.

Plan amendment required mid-build — Phase 4 review forced a PageHeader contract amendment (`level?: 1|2`, default 1) to resolve the h1/h2 conflict without touching protected assertions. The amendment was not a spec gap but a design decision that broke existing contracts — a reconciliation step in Phase 1 would have caught it (Plan reconciliation row: 'design wants h2; existing tests assert h1 — resolution?').

Multi-phase review model proved essential — Phase 2 critique (gate scoping) caught design flaws before code. Phase 4 code review (fresh-context) caught regression mislabeling and forced a correct fix. Neither phase alone would have surfaced the full set of issues: Phase 2 missed the h1/h2 protected-test conflict (design ratification gates did not audit against existing assertions); Phase 4 had to rebuild the fix from scratch because builder's attestation was false.

Spec AC5 re-grounding correct — AC5 promised 'Playwright sweep' but spec revision locked it to 'vitest DOM-snapshot net' per repo policy. Architect correctly re-grounded the AC against the actual verification tool. Snapshot net blessed 8 new PageHeader/SectionLabel variants; enumeration guard bumped 56→58; zero paint regressions silently missed.

Phase 4 fix clean and surgical — builder's response to the two regressions (F1 h1→h2, F2 testid relocation) was correct: amended PageHeader contract to default level=1 (preserving protected assertions verbatim), restored testid to scroll body (restoring AG1 assertions). No collateral changes, no forced-green assertions, no unsafe casts. Attestation re-run honest: 5742/5742 tests green, zero failures.

Recurring pattern: builder attestation false-positives on protected tests. This workpackage mirrors CC-004 water-line — tests can be green on fabricated data while production entrypoints stay dead. Here, the fabrication is inverted: 5 tests were actually red because the implementation broke protected contracts, but attestation mislabeled them pre-existing. A pre-attestation gate that actually runs affected protected-test files would catch this (current flow: builder attest locally → Phase 3 commit → Phase 4 fresh-context reveals). Consider: attestation MUST run the protected-tests list, not just the workpackage's test files.

Cost signal: Phase 4 re-review + fix + re-attest consumed ~2h of wall-clock time and required a second review round. This is the gate's protective value — it prevented a red-build merge. However, the false attestation suggests builder discipline gaps: did the builder skip running the specific test files the implementation touched? Did they skip testing protected-test files by name? Phase 3 should require: 'npm run test WorkProduct.test.tsx WorkRoutine.AA1.test.tsx WorkTeam.AG1.test.tsx' as a pre-attestation step when those files exist in the protected list.
